content.text: Yes—there are proxies that explicitly support both TUIs. The key compatibility detail is that current Codex needs the Responses API; an older proxy offering only Chat Completions won’t work.

**Yes—via an unofficial local proxy.** Projects exist specifically to let both TUIs use your GitHub Copilot subscription.

The setup looks like:

```text
Claude Code ── Anthropic Messages API ─┐
                                      ├─ local proxy ── GitHub Copilot
Codex CLI ──── OpenAI Responses API ───┘
```

[**voidsteed/copilot-proxy-api**](https://github.com/voidsteed/copilot-proxy-api) explicitly documents both integrations, GitHub authentication, and model discovery. It’s a fork of [ericc-ch/copilot-api](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api), whose documented endpoints cover Claude Code but lack the Responses endpoint current Codex needs.

| TUI | How you connect it |
|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | Point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the proxy, configure its credential, and select an available Claude model. [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect) |
| **Codex** | Define a custom `model_provider` with the proxy’s `/v1` URL and `wire_api = "responses"`. Current Codex **doesn’t support `wire_api = "chat"`**, so older tutorials can mislead you. [OpenAI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models#other-models) |

You keep the actual CLI’s interface and local agent tools; the proxy supplies the model backend. You’re limited to models your Copilot account exposes. The proxy also documents compatibility gaps around thinking output, caching, and provider-hosted tools, so expect some differences from direct service access. It’s unofficial and can break when GitHub changes its API. [Project documentation](https://github.com/voidsteed/copilot-proxy-api)

**My take:** that fork is a concrete candidate to try for your existing Codex/Claude Code workflow, though I haven’t tested it against your account. For your dotfiles, I’d make separate `codex-copilot` and `claude-copilot` launchers so switching backends is explicit.

If you mainly want a terminal agent covered by your subscription, **GitHub’s own Copilot CLI is included** and avoids needing this bridge. [GitHub plans](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans)
